story_title: Trading Signals and Returns Analysis: June to July 2009
story_subtitle: Evaluating the performance of short, long, and neutral trading signals across a 62-day period

story_pieces.narration: Short signals had an average return of 3.2946%, while long signals had an average return of -0.9587%. Neutral signals showed no directional movement.
story_pieces.question: How do the average returns of short, long, and neutral trading signals compare?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (signal type vs. average return)

story_pieces.narration: The highest single-day return of 15.49% occurred on June 22, 2009, while the lowest return of -10.84% was recorded on July 17, 2009.
story_pieces.question: Which dates produced the highest and lowest returns, and what patterns exist in extreme return events?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (date vs. return with highlight markers)

story_pieces.narration: Short signals generated no positive returns, while long signals also had no positive returns. Neutral signals showed no directional movement.
story_pieces.question: How do the distribution of positive and negative returns differ between trading signal types?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (signal type vs. positive/negative return counts)

story_pieces.narration: The cumulative return from all trading signals resulted in a 60.855% gain by July 31, 2009, with the most significant contributions from short signals in June.
story_pieces.question: What was the overall performance trend of the trading strategy over the period, and which months drove the most gains?

story_pieces.narration: Short signals were most frequently issued (24 instances), but long signals generated higher absolute returns in July when market conditions shifted.
story_pieces.question: How did the frequency and effectiveness of trading signals change over time, and what factors might have influenced this?
story_pieces.visualization: time series heat map (date vs. signal type frequency and return magnitude)
